correctness.rationale: For any h and positive initial value, the no-cancellation recurrence gives the exact square criterion from the cited 2026 source. Reducing the initial fraction at p^a||h shows only x0 with p-adic valuation exactly a can cause a defect. The two local polynomials have disjoint roots; their counts follow from quadratic reciprocity and the special primes 2 and 5. Independence via the Chinese remainder theorem yields every probability and exact periodicity. An antecedent of a second or later zero would yield a solution of a quadratic of discriminant -5; its nonsquareness for primes 13,17 mod20 proves global rigidity. A root of the second polynomial gives a positive initial-value witness in all excluded classes. The proof establishes infinite quantifiers; exact checks support local arithmetic but are not treated as universal proof.

value.rationale: The exact product law addresses a natural two-index form of the originating paper’s explicit failure-count distribution problem. The sharp if-and-only-if mod-20 criterion yields the full, all-index distribution for an infinite family, and primes 13 mod20 produce arbitrarily large gaps between the general upper bound and the actual sharp maximum.
